title: Cellular Radio Decode Economics — Lab Notes
body:
Purpose:
Run a lightweight, reproducible sweep of decode latency and wire-cost tradeoffs for typical mobile cellular conditions (3G/LTE/5G) to inform Redwood Optimize default knobs for mobile clients and edge routing policies. This doc is intentionally informal lab notes — records of runs, ascii charts, interpretation, and action items rather than a polished brief.

Summary takeaway (short):
- Under high RTT/low-bandwidth links, token-level latency dominates; quantized models reduce CPU/GPU token time but have diminishing returns on wire cost.
- Aggressive chunking (larger generation chunks) reduces radio wake penalties on 3G/LTE but raises p95 p99 for interactive microturns.
- Payload compression (gzip-level 3) yields ~20–40% bytes savings on text responses with ~0–2ms extra decode/encode CPU overhead — net positive for 3G/LTE.

Test matrix (env):
- Model: open-llm-small-v1 (decoder-only), float16 baseline + 8-bit static quant + int4 simulated path.
- Serving: Dedicated small pool, single GPU instance (A100-sim profile).
- Client network profiles simulated with tc/netem:
    * 3G-like: RTT=120ms, BW=2.0Mbps, loss=1%
    * LTE-like: RTT=40ms, BW=20Mbps, loss=0.5%
    * 5G-like: RTT=12ms, BW=200Mbps, loss=0.1%
- Workloads: short-turn chat (user prompt 20 tokens, response target 40 tokens), long completion (prompt 50, response 400 tokens sampling), embedding call (single 1k-char document).
- Batching/timeout knobs tested: immediate (no batching), sessionized smallbatch (batch window 8ms), greedy-chunk (accumulate 32 tokens), large-chunk (accumulate 128 tokens).

Metrics collected (per-run): p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec server-side, bytes-on-wire (avg response), client wake cycles (wake_count per session), CPU-bound decode ms (proxy), estimated $/100k queries (rough extrapolation).

Representative ascii table (condensed):
| Profile | Chunk | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tps(server) | bytes(resp) | wake/call | est $/100k |
|--------:|:-----:|--------:|--------:|--------:|-----------:|-----------:|---------:|----------:|
| 3G      | immediate | 420   | 980    | 2200   | 2.3        | 6.8k       | 3.0      | 520.0     |
| 3G      | greedy-32 | 260   | 540    | 1200   | 3.1        | 5.6k       | 1.4      | 410.0     |
| 3G      | large-128 | 310  | 680    | 1400   | 2.8        | 4.9k       | 1.1      | 395.0     |
| LTE     | immediate | 140   | 330    | 720    | 4.6        | 6.8k       | 2.0      | 370.0     |
| LTE     | greedy-32 | 100   | 190    | 420    | 6.2        | 5.6k       | 1.1      | 295.0     |
| 5G      | immediate | 60    | 120    | 220    | 8.9        | 6.8k       | 1.0      | 275.0     |
| 5G      | greedy-32 | 44    | 96     | 180    | 10.2       | 5.6k       | 1.0      | 245.0     |

Notes on table: est $/100k is a back-of-envelope combining GPU amortized cost + egress bytes; numbers are synthetic to compare knobs, not billing-ready. bytes(resp) reduces with chunking because fewer handshakes and slightly more compact streaming frames observed.

Packet loss sensitivity (3G case, greedy-32):
- loss 0%: p95 ~ 480ms
- loss 1%: p95 ~ 540ms (+12%)
- loss 3%: p95 ~ 710ms (+48%)
Interpretation: packet loss interacts non-linearly with retransmit windows and streaming chunk sizes. Small chunks are safer in high-loss environments for tail stability, large chunks reduce wake cycles but amplify single-packet failure penalty.

ASCII micro-chart: average p95 vs profile (greedy-32):
3G  : ██████████████████ 540ms
LTE  : ████████████ 190ms
5G   : ████ 96ms

Quantization observations:
- 8-bit static produced ~8–12% decrease in server decode ms with negligible impact to token-level variance; bytes-on-wire unchanged.
- int4 simulated path gave ~18–24% decode improvement but increased variance p99 by ~5–10% (occasional model-path slowdowns).
- Recommendation: expose 8-bit as default in mobile routing; reserve int4 for non-interactive long completions where throughput matters more than p99 micro-interactions.

Compression and wire encoding:
- gzip-level 3 reduced bytes(resp) by 22–38% depending on verbosity and presence of markup. CPU cost measured ~0.5–2.0ms per request at server-side (single-threaded encode).
- For 3G/LTE profiles, compression wins in both latency (fewer bytes transmitted, less retransmit exposure) and estimated cost due to egress. For 5G, tradeoffs are neutral-to-negative if server CPU is the bottleneck.

Client warm/keepalive behavior:
- Wake penalty (radio tail) on 3G causes 2–3 extra RTT-equivalent costs if session isn't kept alive between microturns.
- Recommendation: use a short keepalive (200–400ms) window for chat microturns to amortize radio tail; for background embeddings, close aggressively. Redwood Optimize could suggest keepalive per route based on measured microturn spacing.

Suggested Redwood Optimize knob defaults for mobile-targeted routes (initial hypothesis):
- network_profile: auto-detect via client-reported RTT/BW, fallback to 'lte' if unknown.
- default_quant: 8bit for mobile-tier; int4 disabled unless 'bulk' workload flagged.
- streaming_chunk_size: greedy-32 for chat; large-128 for long completions behind background routes.
- compression: enabled for 'mobile' profile (gzip level 3) unless server CPU saturation > 60%.
- keepalive_ms: 300ms for interactive routes; 50ms for handshake/realtime voice.

Open questions / caveats:
- Tests run on a single model + single hardware profile; results may shift with larger models, different kernels, or other GPUs. Need a follow-up sweep on an L/XL class model.
- Egress cost model here is approximate; need product billing inputs to finalize $/100k.
- int4 production path currently experimental (PR #887) — monitor p99 regressions before enabling broadly.

Action items (next 6 weeks):
- [Benji] Run identical sweep on a 6B-12B model family and produce delta sheet (JIRA-OPT-342).
- [Claire] Add a small harness in the perf harness to auto-run packet-loss grid (0/0.5/1/3/5%) and produce p95 heatmap.
- [Marco] Prototype a Redwood Optimize suggestion card: 'mobile-lite' that flips quant=8bit + compression + greedy-32.
- [SRE Rotation] Track GPU CPU saturation while compression is enabled to validate recommendation.

Appendix: compact run log sample (timestamps local)
- 2026-11-08T09:12 — started 3G sweeps, notes: queueing observed at 1.3x baseline during large-128 runs
- 2026-11-10T11:45 — tested gzip l3 vs none; added instrumentation for server encode time
- 2026-11-15T16:30 — int4 sim path added; observed occasional p99 blips correlated with kernel fallback

Loose heuristics for product copy (one-liners):
- 'For mobile users on cellular links, compact streaming and gzip reduce perceived latency and egress cost — we recommend 8-bit quantization + 32-token chunking for chat flows.'

Notes to self: include a horizontal delta chart showing bytes vs p95 for each profile in the follow-up. Save raw traces under: s3://perf-raw/mobile/decode/2026-11-08/ (TODO: permission check).

End of lab notes.
